answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake bonded to a public beacon of past work: completed jobs, signed receipts, and peer attestations accumulate over time, so a new identity starts at the nadir of trust and earns higher rate limits only as its record grows. A haven for cheap clones disappears because spinning up thousands of fresh identities costs stake each time yet buys no reputation, while an attacker who misbehaves forfeits the bond and must rebuild from zero.
